ipak <- function(pkg){
  new.pkg <- pkg[!(pkg %in% installed.packages()[, "Package"])]
  if (length(new.pkg))
    install.packages(new.pkg, dependencies = TRUE)
  sapply(pkg, require, character.only = TRUE)
}

              "rnaturalearthdata","maptiles","tidyverse")

## Clean and prepare

```{r}
# helper: get a column as a vector, or NA if it doesn't exist
getcol <- function(x, name) {
  if (name %in% names(x)) x[[name]] else rep(NA, nrow(x))
}

# 1. plain tibble from `tracks` (lat/long are already ordinary columns)
tracks_df <- tibble(
  deployment_id = as.character(tracks[["deployment_id"]]),
  dt            = as.POSIXct(tracks[["timestamp"]], tz = "UTC"),
  long          = as.numeric(tracks[["long"]]),
  lat           = as.numeric(tracks[["lat"]]),
  sensor        = as.character(getcol(tracks, "sensor_type_id")),
  argos_lc      = as.character(getcol(tracks, "argos_lc")),
  visible       = as.logical(getcol(tracks, "visible")),
  man_out       = as.logical(getcol(tracks, "manually_marked_outlier")),
  alg_out       = as.logical(getcol(tracks, "algorithm_marked_outlier"))
)

# 2. animal ID per deployment, from the reference data
ids <- tibble(
  deployment_id = as.character(meta[["deployment_id"]]),
  ID            = as.character(getcol(meta, "individual_local_identifier"))
) %>%
  distinct(deployment_id, .keep_all = TRUE)

# 3. join and clean
data <- tracks_df %>%
  left_join(ids, by = "deployment_id") %>%
  mutate(ID = coalesce(ID, deployment_id)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(lat), !is.na(long), !is.na(dt),
         !(lat == 0 & long == 0),
         visible %in% c(TRUE, NA),               # drop fixes hidden in Movebank
         !(man_out %in% TRUE),                   # manually marked outliers
         !(alg_out %in% TRUE),                   # algorithm-marked outliers
         is.na(argos_lc) | argos_lc != "Z") %>%  # worst Argos class; GPS rows (NA) are kept
  select(ID, dt, lat, long, sensor, argos_lc) %>%
  distinct(ID, dt, .keep_all = TRUE)

# OPTIONAL: GPS only (Argos is much less precise)
# data <- data %>% filter(sensor == "gps")

# 4. resample to 1 fix per hour (closest fix to each full hour)
data <- data %>%
  mutate(dt_hr     = round_date(dt, "1 hour"),
         dt_offset = abs(as.numeric(difftime(dt, dt_hr, units = "mins")))) %>%
  group_by(ID, dt_hr) %>%
  slice_min(dt_offset, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(-dt_hr, -dt_offset) %>%
  arrange(ID, dt) %>%
  mutate(yr  = year(dt),
         mth = factor(month(dt, label = TRUE, abbr = TRUE)))

# checks
nrow(tracks_df); nrow(data)
sum(is.na(ids$ID))     # deployments without an animal ID in meta
count(data, sensor)
data %>% count(ID, yr) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = yr, values_from = n)
```

## Map 2: one patchwork per individual (one map per year)

Each individual gets its own map extent. The same extent is used for all of its years, so the panels are directly comparable. Routes are coloured by month, so you can see timing within a year.

```{r}
#| label: map-per-individual
# make one year-map for one individual
map_one_year <- function(df, yr_i, xlim, ylim){
  d <- filter(df, yr == yr_i)
  ggplot()+
    geom_sf(data=world,fill='grey60',col='grey85',linewidth=.1)+
    geom_path(data=d,aes(x=long,y=lat,col=mth,group=1),linewidth=.3)+
    geom_point(data=d,aes(x=long,y=lat,col=mth),size=.4,shape=16)+
    scale_colour_viridis_d("Month",option="turbo",drop=FALSE)+
    coord_sf(xlim=xlim,ylim=ylim,expand=FALSE)+
    theme_classic()+
    theme(panel.background=element_rect(fill='grey85'))+
    guides(col=guide_legend(override.aes=list(size=3,linewidth=1)))
    ggtitle(yr_i)+xlab("")+ylab("")
}

# patchwork of all years for one individual
map_individual <- function(df, id){
  years <- sort(unique(df$yr))
  padx  <- max(0.5, diff(range(df$long)) * 0.05)
  pady  <- max(0.5, diff(range(df$lat))  * 0.05)
  xlim  <- range(df$long) + c(-padx, padx)
  ylim  <- range(df$lat)  + c(-pady, pady)

  plots <- map(years, ~ map_one_year(df, .x, xlim, ylim))
  ncols <- min(length(years), 3)

  wrap_plots(plots, ncol = ncols, guides = "collect") +
    plot_annotation(title = paste("Individual:", id)) &
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
}

# loop over all individuals: draw, and save as PNG
by.id <- split(data, data$ID)

for(id in names(by.id)){
  p <- map_individual(by.id[[id]], id)
  print(p)

  n.years <- n_distinct(by.id[[id]]$yr)
  ncols   <- min(n.years, 3)
  nrows   <- ceiling(n.years / ncols)
  fname   <- str_replace_all(id, "[^A-Za-z0-9_-]", "_")   # IDs may contain "/" etc.

 # ggsave(file.path(dir.out, "maps", "per-individual", paste0("Map_", fname, "_per-year.png")),
         p, width = 9 * ncols, height = 8 * nrows, units = "cm", dpi = 300)
}
```

# Part 2: migration start/end, distance, duration, route counts

This part continues from `data.route` (hourly fixes, with `ID_clean`, `route`, `yr`, `dt`, `lat`, `long`).
Everything below is **autumn migration** (breeding area -> wintering area). Tweak the parameters in the first chunk and re-run.

```{r}
#| label: extra-packages
#| results: hide
ipak(c("patchwork", "lme4", "lmerTest", "geodata"))
```

## 1. Helpers, parameters and a speed filter

The straight lines crossing the Sahara/Mediterranean in your maps are almost certainly gaps or bad Argos fixes. They would inflate every distance, so I remove fixes that imply an impossible speed.

```{r}
#| label: helpers

# ---- parameters you may want to tweak --------------------------------------
V_MAX        <- 120   # km/h, faster steps are treated as location errors
R_DEPART     <- 100   # km from summer site: inside = "still at the breeding area"
R_ARRIVE     <- 250   # km from winter site: inside = "arrived at wintering area"
MIN_DIST     <- 500   # km, bird must get at least this far from the summer site to count as migrant
MIN_FIX      <- 20    # minimum fixes needed to define a summer / winter site
AUT_START    <- "08-01"   # autumn window start (month-day)
SUMMER_START <- "06-01"; SUMMER_END <- "07-15"
WINTER_START <- "12-15"; WINTER_END <- "02-15"   # ends in the following year
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# great-circle distance in km (haversine), vectorised
hav_km <- function(lon1, lat1, lon2, lat2){
  r <- 6371.0088; k <- pi / 180
  a <- sin((lat2 - lat1) * k / 2)^2 +
       cos(lat1 * k) * cos(lat2 * k) * sin((lon2 - lon1) * k / 2)^2
  2 * r * asin(pmin(1, sqrt(a)))
}

# add step length (km), time between fixes (h) and speed (km/h), per individual
add_steps <- function(df){
  df %>%
    group_by(ID_clean) %>%
    arrange(dt, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
    mutate(step_km = hav_km(lag(long), lag(lat), long, lat),
           step_h  = as.numeric(difftime(dt, lag(dt), units = "hours")),
           speed   = step_km / step_h) %>%
    ungroup()
}

# drop fixes with impossible incoming speed; repeat because removing one fix changes the next step
remove_speed_outliers <- function(df, vmax = V_MAX, max_iter = 10){
  for(i in seq_len(max_iter)){
    df  <- add_steps(df)
    bad <- which(df$speed > vmax)
    if(length(bad) == 0) break
    df  <- df[-bad, ]
  }
  add_steps(df)
}

n_before <- nrow(data.route)
trk <- remove_speed_outliers(data.route)
n_before - nrow(trk)     # number of fixes removed
```

## 2. Start and end of autumn migration (per individual and year)

Logic, so you can defend it in the methods:

* **Summer site** = median position 1 Jun - 15 Jul of that year (nestlings and breeders sit at the nest then).
* **Winter site** = median position 15 Dec - 15 Feb (birds are settled, or at least much less mobile).
* **Departure** = last fix inside `R_DEPART` km of the summer site after 1 Aug (the bird does not return afterwards).
* **Arrival** = first fix after departure within `R_ARRIVE` km of the winter site.
* Birds that never get further than `MIN_DIST` km from the summer site are labelled `resident` (this matters for migratory *tactics*: West-route birds that stay in Iberia/Morocco will land here).

```{r}
#| label: migration-events
mig_one <- function(d, y){
  fail <- function(msg) tibble(yr = y, status = msg)
  mk   <- function(md, yy = y) ymd(paste0(yy, "-", md), tz = "UTC")

  summer <- filter(d, dt >= mk(SUMMER_START), dt <= mk(SUMMER_END) + days(1))
  winter <- filter(d, dt >= mk(WINTER_START), dt <= mk(WINTER_END, y + 1) + days(1))
  if(nrow(summer) < MIN_FIX) return(fail("no summer fixes"))
  if(nrow(winter) < MIN_FIX) return(fail("no winter fixes"))

  s_lon <- median(summer$long); s_lat <- median(summer$lat)
  w_lon <- median(winter$long); w_lat <- median(winter$lat)

  aut <- d %>%
    filter(dt >= mk(AUT_START), dt < mk("01-01", y + 1)) %>%
    mutate(d_sum = hav_km(s_lon, s_lat, long, lat))
  if(nrow(aut) == 0)                return(fail("no autumn fixes"))
  if(max(aut$d_sum) < MIN_DIST)     return(fail("resident"))

  in_idx <- which(aut$d_sum <= R_DEPART)
  if(length(in_idx) == 0)           return(fail("no fixes at summer site in autumn"))
  dep <- aut[max(in_idx), ]

  post <- d %>%
    filter(dt >= dep$dt) %>%
    mutate(d_win = hav_km(w_lon, w_lat, long, lat))
  arr_i <- which(post$d_win <= R_ARRIVE)
  if(length(arr_i) == 0)            return(fail("never reached winter site"))
  arr   <- post[min(arr_i), ]

  # the actual migration track (first row's step comes from before departure, so drop it)
  m <- filter(d, dt >= dep$dt, dt <= arr$dt) %>% slice(-1)
  if(nrow(m) < 2)                   return(fail("too few fixes in migration"))

  dist_km  <- sum(m$step_km, na.rm = TRUE)
  dur_d    <- as.numeric(difftime(arr$dt, dep$dt, units = "days"))
  straight <- hav_km(dep$long, dep$lat, arr$long, arr$lat)

  # in-flight speed from well-sampled steps only -> estimated flight hours
  ok       <- m$step_h <= 1.5 & m$step_km >= 10
  v_flight <- mean(m$speed[ok], na.rm = TRUE)

  # travel days = days with > 50 km covered
  travel_days <- m %>% mutate(day = as_date(dt)) %>%
    group_by(day) %>% summarise(km = sum(step_km, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    filter(km > 50) %>% nrow()

  tibble(yr = y, status = "complete",
         dep_time = dep$dt, dep_lon = dep$long, dep_lat = dep$lat,
         arr_time = arr$dt, arr_lon = arr$long, arr_lat = arr$lat,
         summer_lon = s_lon, summer_lat = s_lat,
         winter_lon = w_lon, winter_lat = w_lat,
         dist_km = dist_km, straight_km = straight,
         straightness = straight / dist_km,           # 1 = perfectly direct
         duration_d = dur_d, travel_days = travel_days,
         speed_km_d = dist_km / dur_d,                # overall pace incl. stopovers
         km_per_travel_day = dist_km / travel_days,   # pace on days actually travelling
         fly_hours = dist_km / v_flight,              # estimated hours in flight
         max_gap_h = max(m$step_h, na.rm = TRUE),     # data-quality flag
         n_fix = nrow(m))
}

mig <- trk %>%
  group_by(ID_clean, route) %>%
  group_modify(~ map_dfr(sort(unique(.x$yr)), \(y) mig_one(.x, y))) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  group_by(ID_clean) %>%
  mutate(first_year = yr == min(yr)) %>%     # first autumn of that bird (valid if tagged as nestling)
  ungroup()

# how many individual-years made it into the analysis, and why the others dropped out
count(mig, status, sort = TRUE)

mig_ok <- mig %>%
  filter(status == "complete") %>%
  mutate(dep_doy = yday(dep_time),
         arr_doy = yday(arr_time),
         route   = factor(route, levels = c("West", "East")))

# sanity checks: very short routes or big data gaps deserve a look
mig_ok %>% filter(max_gap_h > 72 | dist_km < 800) %>%
  select(ID_clean, yr, route, dist_km, duration_d, max_gap_h)
```

## 3. Distance and duration of each route

```{r}
# which migrations have no flight-hour estimate? (sparse fixes)
mig_ok %>% filter(!is.finite(fly_hours)) %>%
  select(ID_clean, yr, route, n_fix, max_gap_h)

route_summary <- mig_ok %>%
  group_by(route) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), n_ind = n_distinct(ID_clean),
            across(c(dist_km, duration_d, travel_days, fly_hours, speed_km_d, km_per_travel_day, straightness),
                   list(median = ~median(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                        q25    = ~quantile(.x, .25, na.rm = TRUE),
                        q75    = ~quantile(.x, .75, na.rm = TRUE)),
                   .names = "{.col}__{.fn}"),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_longer(-c(route, n, n_ind), names_to = c("metric", "stat"), names_sep = "__") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = stat, values_from = value) %>%
  mutate(across(c(median, q25, q75), \(x) round(x, 2)))
route_summary
write_csv(route_summary, file.path(dir.out, "tables", "route_summary.csv"))
```



## 4. How often was each route taken?

```{r}
#| label: route-counts
# individuals and migrations per route
mig_ok %>% group_by(route) %>%
  summarise(migrations = n(), individuals = n_distinct(ID_clean),
            mean_migrations_per_bird = migrations / individuals)

# per year
route_year <- mig_ok %>% count(yr, route) %>%
  complete(yr, route, fill = list(n = 0))
route_year %>% pivot_wider(names_from = route, values_from = n)

ggplot(route_year, aes(factor(yr), n, fill = route)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(West = "#d95f02", East = "#1b9e77")) +
  theme_classic() + xlab("Year") + ylab("Number of completed autumn migrations") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

# do individuals stick to one route?
mig_ok %>% group_by(ID_clean) %>%
  summarise(n_routes = n_distinct(route), n_years = n()) %>%
  count(n_routes, name = "individuals")
```

Because `route` was assigned per individual (your `west.ids` list), the last table will always show 1 route per bird. If you later classify routes per migration (e.g. by which strait is crossed), the same table tells you how many birds switch.

## 5. Departure timing

```{r}
#| label: departure
ref_date <- \(doy) as.Date(doy - 1, origin = "2001-01-01")   # one common year for plotting

# (a) all years pooled
ggplot(mig_ok, aes(ref_date(dep_doy), fill = route)) +
  geom_density(alpha = .5, colour = NA) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(West = "#d95f02", East = "#1b9e77")) +
  scale_x_date(date_labels = "%d %b") +
  theme_classic() + xlab("Departure date") + ylab("Density")

wilcox.test(dep_doy ~ route, data = mig_ok, exact = FALSE)

# pooled model: year and individual as random effects, first-year birds usually leave differently
m_dep <- lmer(dep_doy ~ route + first_year + (1 | yr) + (1 | ID_clean), data = mig_ok)
summary(m_dep)

# (b) within the same year
ggplot(mig_ok, aes(route, ref_date(dep_doy), fill = route)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, alpha = .5) +
  geom_jitter(width = .12, size = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(West = "#d95f02", East = "#1b9e77")) +
  scale_y_date(date_labels = "%d %b") +
  facet_wrap(~yr) +
  theme_classic() + theme(legend.position = "none") + xlab("") + ylab("Departure date")

within_year <- mig_ok %>%
  group_by(yr) %>%
  filter(all(table(route) >= 3)) %>%            # need >= 3 birds per route in that year
  summarise(n_West = sum(route == "West"), n_East = sum(route == "East"),
            med_West = median(dep_doy[route == "West"]),
            med_East = median(dep_doy[route == "East"]),
            diff_days_East_minus_West = med_East - med_West,
            p_wilcox = wilcox.test(dep_doy ~ route, exact = FALSE)$p.value,
            .groups = "drop")
within_year

# overall within-year effect: year as fixed effect, so only same-year comparisons count
lmer(dep_doy ~ route + factor(yr) + (1 | ID_clean), data = mig_ok) %>% summary()
```

## 6. Which route is energetically cheaper?

We have GPS/Argos only (no acceleration, so no ODBA), so energetics has to be inferred from proxies: distance, estimated flight hours (flapping/soaring flight costs scale with time aloft), how direct the route is, and how many days of travelling it takes.

```{r}
#| label: energetics
cost <- mig_ok %>%
  select(ID_clean, yr, route, first_year, dist_km, fly_hours, travel_days,
         duration_d, straightness, km_per_travel_day)

cost %>% group_by(route) %>%
  summarise(across(c(dist_km, fly_hours, travel_days, duration_d, straightness),
                   \(x) round(median(x), 2)))

# model each proxy with the same structure
cost_models <- c("dist_km", "fly_hours", "travel_days", "duration_d", "straightness") %>%
  set_names() %>%
  map(\(v) lmer(reformulate(c("route", "first_year", "(1 | ID_clean)"), response = v), data = cost))

# route effect (East relative to West) for each proxy
map_dfr(cost_models, \(m) as_tibble(coef(summary(m)), rownames = "term") %>%
          filter(term == "routeEast"), .id = "proxy")
```

Caveat to keep in mind when writing it up: if a bird has a long data gap, `dist_km` is a minimum (straight line over the gap). `max_gap_h` in `mig_ok` lets you rerun everything on `filter(max_gap_h <= 48)` as a robustness check.

## 7. Link with the wintering grounds

Hypothesis: the route that costs more energy leads to better wintering grounds. Here the wintering site is the median position of each bird in mid-winter (`winter_lon/lat`). Climate comes from WorldClim (downloads once, then cached in `./output/env`). Annual and winter precipitation are crude proxies for food availability; swap in NDVI or cropland cover when you want something closer to stork habitat.

```{r}
#| label: winter-env
dir.env <- file.path(dir.out, "env"); dir.create(dir.env, showWarnings = FALSE)

prec <- worldclim_global(var = "prec", res = 10, path = dir.env)
names(prec) <- month.abb
prec_year   <- sum(prec)
prec_winter <- sum(prec[[c("Dec", "Jan", "Feb")]])

pts <- vect(select(mig_ok, winter_lon, winter_lat), geom = c("winter_lon", "winter_lat"), crs = "EPSG:4326")

mig_env <- mig_ok %>%
  mutate(prec_year   = terra::extract(prec_year,   pts)[, 2],
         prec_winter = terra::extract(prec_winter, pts)[, 2])

# winter range summary per route
mig_env %>% group_by(route) %>%
  summarise(median_lat = median(winter_lat), median_lon = median(winter_lon),
            prec_year = median(prec_year, na.rm = TRUE),
            prec_winter = median(prec_winter, na.rm = TRUE))

(ggplot(mig_env, aes(route, prec_year, fill = route)) + geom_boxplot(alpha = .5) +
   scale_fill_manual(values = c(West = "#d95f02", East = "#1b9e77")) +
   theme_classic() + theme(legend.position = "none") + xlab("") + ylab("Annual precipitation (mm)")) |
(ggplot(mig_env, aes(route, prec_winter, fill = route)) + geom_boxplot(alpha = .5) +
   scale_fill_manual(values = c(West = "#d95f02", East = "#1b9e77")) +
   theme_classic() + theme(legend.position = "none") + xlab("") + ylab("Dec-Feb precipitation (mm)"))

lmer(prec_year ~ route + (1 | ID_clean), data = mig_env) %>% summary()
```

### Cost versus benefit

```{r}
#| label: cost-benefit
# crude "payoff" proxy: how long each bird was followed after the first migration
# (confounded by tag failure, so treat with care)
years_tracked <- trk %>% group_by(ID_clean) %>%
  summarise(years_tracked = as.numeric(difftime(max(dt), min(dt), units = "days")) / 365.25)

cb <- mig_env %>% left_join(years_tracked, by = "ID_clean")

ggplot(cb, aes(fly_hours, prec_year, colour = route)) +
  geom_point(alpha = .6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(West = "#d95f02", East = "#1b9e77")) +
  theme_classic() +
  xlab("Cost: estimated flight hours") + ylab("Benefit: annual precipitation at wintering site (mm)")

cb %>% distinct(ID_clean, route, years_tracked) %>%
  group_by(route) %>% summarise(n = n(), median_years_tracked = median(years_tracked))
```
